la:noun:amentia.gloss: madness, insanity (the state of being out of one's senses)
senses: madness, insanity (the state of being out of one's senses)
la:noun:amentia.html:
āmentĭa, ae, f.
amens
,
the being out of one's senses, beside one's self, madness, insanity.
Lit.: animi adfectionem lumine mentis carentem nominaverunt amentiam eandemque dementiam,: Di monerint meliora atque amentiam averruncassint tuam, Pac. ap. Müll., and in Paul. ex Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 90 Rib.): heu cor ira fervit caecum, amentiā rapior ferorque, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 194 Rib.): Quor meam senectutem hujus sollicito amentiā,: Quae istast pravitas, Quaeve amentiast ...?; (not elsewhere in Ter.): flagrare cupiditate atque amentiā,: amentiā atque audaciā praeditus,; : tanta vis amentiae verius quam amoris mentem turbaverat,; : Percutiat te Dominus amentiā,; .—
Meton.
Folly, stupidity (cf. amens, II.): si quem amentia verset,.—
Malice, malignity (eccl. Lat.): propter multitudinem amentiae (tuae),.

la:adj:amens.html:
ā-mens, mentis, adj.
Lit., out of one's senses, beside one's self, senseless, mad, insane, frantic, distracted (of every kind of passionate excitement; while insanus designates one diseased in mind; and excors or vecors, one that is without mind; among the poets a favorite word with Verg. and Ov.): inceptio est amentium, haud amantium,: homo amentissimus atque in omnibus consiliis praeceps,: o vecors et amens,: arma amens capio,: in dies amentior,: Ne trepides caeli divisis partibus amens,that thou tremble not senselessly at the divided heavens,: lugubris et amens,: cursuque amens,: adspectu amens,; so ; and with gen.: amens animi, (cf. Rudd. II. p. 73): dolore amens,: terrore amens,: amens invidiā,: amens metu,; : periculi magnitudine amens et attonitus,.—
Meton., foolish, stupid: homo audacissimus atque amentissimus, (cf. a little before: quod cum incredibili ejus audaciā singularis stultitia conjuncta est).—Of things: amentissimum consilium,: cogor amenti caeca furore,: impetus amens,—Adv. not used.

la:verb:amento.gloss: to furnish with a strap or thong
senses: to furnish with a strap or thong
to hurl, dart or speed on something by using or as if by using a thong
la:verb:amento.html:
āmento, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
amentum
.
Lit., to furnish with a strap or thong; esp. of the javelin, to the middle of which a strap was fastened, so that it might be thrown with greater force (very rare; only twice in Cic.): hastae amentatae,.—Trop., of discourse: amentatae hastae (i. e. apta et parata argumenta), (so Juv. sagittae and jaculator, q. v.).—Hence,
Transf., poet., to hurl or dart the javelin by means of a thong: cum jaculum parvā Libysamentavit habenā, * .—And of the wind, which gives an impetus to motion, as a thong to the dart: amentante Noto,.

la:noun:ames.gloss: a pole; a fork for spreading nets
senses: a pole; a fork for spreading nets
la:noun:ames.html:
ămĕs, ĭtis, prob. m.
cf. amentum
,
a pole or fork, esp. for holding and spreading bird-nets: amites: perticae aucupales, Paul. ex Müll.: aut amite levi rara tendit retia, * ; . —Also for bearing a litter or sedan: amites basternarum,.

la:noun:amentum.gloss: A strap or thong, especially one used to propel a spear or other missile weapon
senses: A strap or thong, especially one used to propel a spear or other missile weapon
la:noun:amentum.html:
āmentum, i, n.
ἅμμα, ἅπτω; v. apo
,
a strap or thong, esp. upon missile weapons, by means of which they were thrown with greater force (cf. amento): amenta, quibus, ut mitti possint, vinciuntur jacula sive solearum lora, Paul. ex Müll.: epistola ad amentum deligata, Herz.: inserit amento digitos,: amenta torquent,: umor jaculorum amenta emollierat,—Rarely, a shoe-string: soleae sine amento,.

la:adv:amen.gloss: amen; so be it, let it be
senses: amen; so be it, let it be
la:adv:amen.html:
āmēn
; Gr. ἀμήν
(eccl. Lat.).
Adj., true, faithful: (tu Deus) fecisti mirabilia, cogitationes fideles, amen (Heb. = verity), .—
Subst., truth, faith fulness: qui benedictus est, benedicetur in Deo amen,in the God of faithfulness,: haec dicit Amen (Gr. ὁ Αμήν), He that is True, .—
Most freq. adv.
Prop., to confirm words spoken by one's self or another, So be it; Fr. Ainsi soit-il; LXX. γένοιτο, Amen: et respondebit omnis populus, Amen,; et saep.: Gratia vobiscum, Amen,: cui (Deo) honor et gloria in saecula saeculorum, Amen, et saep. —
In gen., truly, surely, verily; very freq. in the phrase. Amen dico vobis, Vulg. Matt. 5, 18 al.; ; ; and in St. John: Amen, amen dico vobis, (The a is long in Aus. Eph. ap. Orat. fin., and , but short in Paul. Nol. Poëm. 17 ad Nicet. 117.)

la:other:Ameria.gloss: an ancient city in Umbria, now Amelia
senses: an ancient city in Umbria, now Amelia
la:other:Ameria.html:
Ămĕrĭa, ae, f., = Ἀμερία,
a very ancient town in Umbria (acc. to Cato, built

before the Trojan war), now Amelia, ; —Hence, ămĕrīnus, a, um, adj., of or pertaining to Ameria: municeps,: corbulae,: salix,; ; — ămĕrīni, ōrum, m., the inhabitants of Ameria, .—ămĕrīna, ōrum, n. (sc. mala or pira), Amerian fruit, .
